High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible Around high tide 
We are entering a sequence of Spring tides that may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible around 06:45 on Friday 11th September. Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. The first high tide is at 06:45 on Friday with a peak height of 6.12m and a F4 north westerly wind. The second high tide is at 19:00 on Friday with a peak height of 6.37m and a F4 westerly wind 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 12:19PM on 10 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.description: Tidal River Avon at Bristol, Pill and Shirehampton

floodArea.county: City of Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire

items.message:
High tides this evening may lead to flooding.

Flooding is possible from 09:00PM to 11:00PM on 13/09.

Areas most at risk include the tidal River Avon from Sea Mills to Conham in Bristol and between the Avonmouth Bridge and Shirehampton Park including Pill and Shirehampton. 

We are closely monitoring the situation.

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.

This message will be updated by 2:00PM on 14/09 or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham to Breydon Water
items.message:
High river levels today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible today, Sunday, 13th September. 
We expect to see high water levels at Beccles Quay. River levels will remain high over the next couple of days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . Avoid using low lying footpaths which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 14 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.description: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
items.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 12:45pm and 2:45pm today, Sunday 13th September. 
Clacton Promenade, Lee-over-Sands and Brightlingsea sea front may see some wave overtopping and spray. The Strood at Mersea Island, Coast Road and car parks on the front at West Mersea, and the Hythe and Promenade at Maldon may be flooded. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Clacton of 2.76mAODN at 1:45pm, on Sunday 13th September, which is 0.14m above tide tables, wind force 3, south westerly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on 14 September 2026 or as the situation changes.
